applies_why: This judge text counts Matthew 1:18 and Matthew 1:25 toward a broken link without quoting an earlier-round sentence that pressed them or naming that round.
quote: D2 vs C3 (Matthew 1:18, 25): CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" and Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" contradict C3's claim of espousal union; [L2] πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν (prin ē synelthein, Strong's G4250/G4905, before coming together) and οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν (ouk eginōsken, Strong's G1097, was not knowing); [L3] Luke 1:34.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. A verse the judge says was answered is not counted.
room: A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way — reading one: K-G4 applies to any verse counted toward a broken link; reading two: K-G4 applies only when the judge expressly discusses a 'cited in' line.
why: Because the judge treats Matthew 1:18 and Matthew 1:25 as support for a broken link but names no earlier round and quotes no pressing sentence, K-G4 is not satisfied.
